evidence_tree.method: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

independent_computation.step_1_what_the_leaf_means: The rotation receipt is {order, setup, rationale} (data/worklists/f2-task.md deliverable 4; f3-task.md 1a defines 'setup/consume edges'). '/fights/manual_target/rotation/setup' is therefore the ordered setup-phase cast list — the applier casts that must precede their consumers. setup[1] is the second setup cast.
independent_computation.step_2_who_is_the_setup_ability: From the cached wiki text, Dark Sphere (Q) is Syndra's only applier: 'Syndra conjures a Dark Sphere at the target location ... The Dark Sphere then remains on the ground for 6 seconds.' All three of her other actives consume a live sphere: W 'telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere ... Grabbing prioritizes Dark Spheres'; E 'Dark Spheres can be knocked back ... Targets hit are also stunned'; R 'conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones'. So every setup entry for Syndra must be Q, and at least one is required.
independent_computation.step_3_how_many_setup_casts_are_sourced_: The scenario pins the splinters option at 120 (data/champion-audit/batch-6.json: 'splinters option (0-120)'; data/champions.json P: stacks 'up to 120 times'). At 120 splinters every Transcendent threshold is met, including Q's: 'Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 40 Splinters of Wrath causes Syndra to periodically stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2.' Two stocked charges = exactly two back-to-back Dark Sphere casts available in the setup phase, hence setup = [Q, Q] and setup[1] = 'Q'.
independent_computation.step_4_why_not_three_or_more: The charge cap is explicitly 'a maximum of 2'. A third sphere requires waiting a full recharge: Q cooldown/rechargeRate = 7 s at every rank with affectedByCdr = false; only R's passive reduces it ('Dark Sphere's cooldown is reduced equivalent to an amount of ability haste', 10/20/30 by R rank), giving 7 x 100/(100+AH) = 6.364 / 5.833 / 5.385 s. That exceeds any burst setup window (Q castTime 'none', E castTime 0.25 s, R castTime 0.25 s), so 2 is both the ceiling and the value at 120 splinters.
independent_computation.step_5_why_the_second_sphere_is_strictly: R's per-sphere row is 80/120/160 (+20% AP) and the min/max rows are internally consistent with a strictly additive sphere count: 3 x per-sphere = 240/360/480 (+60% AP) = the 'Minimum Magic Damage' row (0 live spheres, 3 conjured); 7 x per-sphere = 560/840/1120 (+140% AP) = the 'Maximum Magic Damage' row (3 conjured + 4 grabbed). Verified arithmetic at all three ranks. Each pre-laid live sphere is therefore worth exactly per-sphere damage with no diminishing term up to 4, so the optimal setup lays every sphere the charge system allows. Going from one setup Q (4 spheres in R) to two (5 spheres) adds 160 + 20% AP raw magic damage at R rank 3.
independent_computation.conclusion: A setup list of length 2 whose second element is the Dark Sphere cast 'Q' is the value the cached source data supports at splinters = 120. The old state — setup index 1 absent, i.e. a single sphere laid — ignores the sourced 40-splinter second charge and under-fills R (4 spheres instead of 5, a 160 + 20% AP shortfall at R3).

caveats: The oracle worked only from data/ and docs/math-foundations.md; the scenario definition and the rotation resolver source were deliberately not read, so the label used for the second charge is judged on the source data alone. If the engine elsewhere addresses the second charge by the synthetic slot key 'Q2', a golden label of 'Q' is a naming question, not a value error — the sourced fact (a second Dark Sphere cast is available and optimal in the setup phase at 120 splinters) holds either way.
